clue.text: Develop friend as top-class rodent catcher

indicators.note: a catcher holds something inside it, so the friend word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class or top-drawer

explanation.surface: A pal turns out to be a first-rate ratcatcher, developing new skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'top-class' gives U from the old British U and non-U division of upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To maturate is to ripen or develop, a rather formal verb for growing to maturity.

clue.text: Man shortly to tour America in charge of show

indicators.note: touring goes all round, so the shortened man word encloses the rest
shortly cuts the final letter off the man word

explanation.surface: A man briefly travels across the United States running a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man shortly' is a man word with its last letter cut, not an abbreviation of man itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show with songs.

clue.text: Drink provided by the van regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words the van, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Refreshments are supplied by a catering van.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink made from infused leaves.

clue.text: Mites sped with derris being sprayed

indicators.note: being sprayed scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Garden pests rush off as the insecticide derris is sprayed on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Derris is a garden insecticide, which keeps the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Red spiders are tiny plant-feeding mites, the red spider mite.

clue.text: Return of bad mood with part of one's mind lacking enthusiasm

indicators.note: return means the bad mood word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
in Freudian theory the id is part of the psyche

explanation.surface: A sulk returns, along with a mental state that is half-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid, literally lukewarm, also means half-hearted or unenthusiastic.

clue.text: Fruit around front of synagogue for Jewish festival

indicators.note: the fruit word goes round the next piece, enclosing it
the front of a word is its opening letter, here from synagogue

explanation.surface: Fruit is laid out around the synagogue entrance for a religious holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesach is the Hebrew name for Passover, the spring Jewish holiday.

clue.text: The water? That may be poured from this

definitions.text: The water? That may be poured from this

indicators.note: pouring something out of a container removes it, so the letters of that leave the letters of the water

explanation.surface: A riddle: what jug might water be poured from?
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H, A, T in order from THEWATER and EWER is left; the whole clue also describes a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: An ewer is a large jug from which water is poured into a basin.

clue.text: Hymn request certainly not coming from Greta Garbo

definitions.text: Hymn request certainly not coming from Greta Garbo

parts.words: Hymn request certainly not coming from Greta Garbo
parts.note: a hymn whose title asks for company, the opposite of the famous plea to be left alone

explanation.walkthrough: Garbo is famed for the line 'I want to be alone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known Christian hymn whose title is a plea for company, often sung at funerals.

clue.text: No good act can stop a witch looking guilty

indicators.note: stopping something plugs it, so the pieces sit inside the witch word

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A witch looks shamefaced because a single good deed could halt her.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangdog describes a shamefaced, guilty-looking expression.

clue.text: Traveller's vehicle hiding foot of pillar

indicators.note: hiding the foot removes the last letter of the pillar word

explanation.surface: An explorer's transport conceals the base of a column.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Columbus was a famous voyager and explorer, a celebrated traveller.

clue.text: He does mad pun in act possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the preceding words may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A man performs a crazy wordplay routine on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'does mad pun in act'; 'He' alone is the definition, a performer whose act might well include mad puns.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a bare pronoun standing for a male performer described by the whole clue, an entertainer doing a stage routine.

clue.text: Applauded back in the pavilion, but exhausted

parts.note: in cricket, a dismissed batsman walks back to the pavilion, being out

explanation.surface: A batsman is cheered back to the pavilion but is utterly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The pavilion is the clubhouse at a cricket ground; a batsman who is OUT returns there.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out or broken down, used of machines or tired people.

clue.text: In senate ban disruptive female campaigner

indicators.note: disruptive throws the letters into disorder, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman campaigner causes disruption by challenging a ban in the senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Besant was a British social reformer who campaigned for birth control, Indian home rule and workers' rights.

clue.text: Top actor is shot maybe

definitions.meaning: the principal performer in a play or film, the star role
the metal of bullets and pellets, of which shot is an example

explanation.definitionFit: The star role is the lead, and shot pellets are made of the metal lead.

clue.text: Journey restricted by flimsy source of illumination

indicators.note: being restricted by another word means sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A trip is limited by a weak light source.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip light is a long tubular fluorescent lamp, a light fitting.

clue.text: In a row on account of impudent chat about naughty nude

indicators.note: about means going round, so the chat word surrounds the rearranged letters
naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so the word nude is rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over someone's cheeky remarks about a racy nude picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a row' looks like a quarrel but means arranged in a line, and 'on account of' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Things lined up stand one after another in a straight line, in a row.

clue.text: Rooms in a bad state with plaster finally falling in

indicators.note: falling in drops a letter inside the other word

parts.note: parlous means in a perilous or bad state

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of plaster

explanation.surface: Rooms are in disrepair as the plaster finally comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlours are sitting rooms in a house.

clue.text: Activity of person hanging around races?

indicators.note: hanging around surrounds, so the person word goes round the races

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Wondering what someone loitering at the racecourse is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are held on the Isle of Man; the whole clue also hints at a punter's pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagering is an activity, a pursuit people engage in, particularly at the races.

clue.text: Person giving attention to sheep primarily?

definitions.text: Person giving attention to sheep primarily?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the word's first letter, here from sheep

parts.note: someone who listens is a hearer

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after sheep before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a shearer gives sheep close attention with the clippers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer clips wool from sheep, so the whole clue describes one at work.

clue.text: Soldier catches any number of fish

indicators.note: catching holds the second piece inside the soldier word

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer, a soldier
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: A soldier hauls in lots of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapper is a food fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Snake gives the woman gash at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the gash word ahead of the woman word

explanation.surface: A snake gives a woman a cut on the front of her body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb here, meaning to slide along.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake and to slither both mean to slide sinuously along the ground.

clue.text: Leftovers I reused in stew

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone recycles leftover food into a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the rest is used or removed.

clue.text: A drug that's not soft? I say!

indicators.note: not soft removes P, the music abbreviation for piano meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drug is soft and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) means soft in music, so 'not soft' takes it out of HEMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is a throat-clearing interjection used to catch attention, like the exclamation I say.

clue.text: Poles are put down by these Italians

definitions.text: Poles are put down by these Italians

parts.words: Poles are put down by these Italians
parts.note: seems to be about Italians disparaging Polish people, but the poles are punting poles thrust down into Venetian canals

explanation.definitionFit: Venetian boatmen propel their craft by pushing long poles down to the canal bed.

clue.text: Tot needs area for play

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a dram

explanation.surface: A small child needs room to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' suggests a child; it is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage.

clue.text: Ignore crossing thoroughfare, having little hesitation backing out

indicators.note: out removes the next piece from the thoroughfare word
backing means the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: er is a brief hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a road crossing and hesitates before reversing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ER into RE, which 'out' removes from STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's instruction to let deleted text stand, ignoring the crossing-out.

clue.text: Emperor's men are radiant group when properly trained

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An emperor's soldiers make a splendid unit once they have been drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Praetorian Guard was the bodyguard of Roman emperors, so its soldiers are the emperor's men.

clue.text: Resistance blocks current discharge

indicators.note: blocking sits inside, so the resistance letter goes inside the current word

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Electrical resistance prevents a current from discharging.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a luminous electrical discharge between two electrodes.

clue.text: Rubbish provided by mischief maker — it's spin

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A troublemaker dismisses something as nonsense: it is just spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like the noun of political PR; it is the verb, to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn round on an axis, the same as to rotate.

clue.text: Humbug used by one semi-intelligent is heard in church

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the intelligent word is used

explanation.surface: Hypocritical talk from a half-witted person is overheard in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant drawn from the Bible, sung during church services.
